findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts:336-349 — releaseProviderProcessSlot now THROWS where main's releaseSlot swallowed errors, but all 6 production call sites invoke it from a bare finally/catch, so a release failure REPLACES the in-flight exception or turns a successful provider run into a hard error. Verified: (a) the new function has no try/catch and calls withProviderRegistryLock (provider-process-registry.ts:267-291), which calls acquireMkdirLock with deadlineMs 30_000; mkdir-lock.ts:306 throws `<label> lock timeout after <ms>ms` on deadline. (b) `git show main:packages/main/src/core/host-run.ts` releaseSlot (line 706) wrapped the entire body in `try { ... } catch { /* Best-effort release; pid-death / the orphan backstop reclaims a leak. */ }`. (c) The smoke deliberately asserts BOTH throw paths — provider-process-registry-smoke.ts:326-334 (injected unlink failure) and :361-370 (`/provider-process-registry lock timeout/`, 'registry-lock mutation failure must reach the supervising owner') — yet no caller supervises it. Call sites: codex-review-leaf.ts:650 and autopilot-executor.ts:413 (bare finally, comments at :647-649 and :410-412 still say 'best-effort (pid-death / the orphan backstop reclaims a leak)'), planned-steps-executor.ts:470 and lattice-dispatch.ts:2484,:2725 (bare finally via releaseProviderProcessAdmission), host-run.ts:1862,:2021 (inside a catch that rethrows). Failure scenario: runCodexReviewLeaf's runner completes successfully and assigns `outcome`; control enters the finally at :648; a concurrent lattice-dispatch/autopilot process holds <slots>.lock for >30s, so acquireMkdirLock throws; per JS semantics a throw from finally discards the completed try block, so runCodexReviewLeaf propagates 'provider-process-registry lock timeout' and the cross-host review verdict that actually ran is reported as a hard error. Same interleaving with a failing runner (e.g. codex ENOENT) replaces the real ENOENT diagnostic with the lock-timeout message. Fix: wrap each release in try/catch (restoring main's best-effort semantics) or make the release failure an explicitly recorded diagnostic that never displaces the primary outcome; and correct the three stale 'best-effort' comments either way.

packages/main/src/core/managed-review-evidence.ts:202,208 — verifyManagedReviewEvidence reads terminal.json and spec.json OUTSIDE its fail-closed try/catch, so a partial runtime directory makes it throw instead of returning the intended diagnostic. The try at :181-199 covers only managedHostRunReceipt / readManagedReviewEvidenceProposal / readManagedHostRunBinding; the very next statements do unguarded `sha256(readFileSync(terminalPath,'utf8'))` (:202) and `sha256(readFileSync(join(runDirectory,'spec.json'),'utf8'))` (:208) plus `readdirSync(runDirectory)` (:206). This is internally inconsistent within the same block: :209 and :212 defensively guard events.jsonl and result.json with existsSync, while terminal.json and spec.json do not. REPRODUCED with a runnable probe: given a run directory retaining spec.json+owner.json but no terminal.json, plus a self-consistent archived receipt under .lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/<runId>.json (so managedHostRunReceipt succeeds via its archive fallback at managed-host-run.ts:2236-2248), the call threw `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '.../host-runs/<runId>/terminal.json'` rather than returning {valid:false}. Reachability correction: the documented GC path is NOT a trigger — pruneExpiredManagedHostRuns calls removeManagedHostRunRuntime (managed-host-run.ts:2446,:2457) which rmSync's the WHOLE directory, so the guarded readManagedHostRunBinding (which reads spec.json, managed-host-run.ts:2045-2046) throws first and is caught. The reachable trigger is partial/corrupt runtime state: an interrupted rmSync, a manual/tooling deletion, or a disk error leaving spec.json while terminal.json is gone. Blast radius is bounded — machine.ts:867-869 catches it and fails closed as `review_verdict_error` — so this is a diagnostic-quality defect, not a gate bypass, but it directly defeats the stated intent of the B-137a:F-107 comment at :186-189 ('surface WHY instead of discarding it'): the operator gets a raw ENOENT stack message instead of the registered managed_receipt_invalid remediation reason. Fix: move :202-214 inside the existing try, or guard terminal.json/spec.json with existsSync exactly as events.jsonl/result.json already are.

packages/main/src/core/codex-review-leaf.ts:619,630-631 and packages/main/src/core/autopilot-executor.ts:363-397 — the provider-admission blocks are misindented so they READ as still ledger-gated, which inverts the exact invariant CHK-004 was written to establish ('Enforce shared provider admission independent of usage-ledger mode'). In codex-review-leaf.ts the admission body sits at 4-space indent inside `if (!opts.managedExecution) {`, but the nested `if (admissionSlot === null) {` at :619 sits at 2-space with its closing brace at :630 also at 2-space. In autopilot-executor.ts the `if (ledgerOn) { ... }` block actually CLOSES at :361, yet the entire '(2) Concurrency admission' block at :363-397 remains indented 4 spaces as if still inside it, and its `if (slot === null)` closes with a 2-space `}` at :397. Both compile (verified: `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/main` exits 0), so this is not a behavioral defect — the failure mode is review/maintenance. Failure scenario: a future maintainer auditing whether admission still runs with LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0 reads autopilot-executor.ts:363, sees the block indented under what appears to be the ledger conditional, and concludes admission is ledger-gated — the precise misreading CHK-004's adversarial:0 intent ('a new direct spawn path must make the contract test fail') exists to prevent. Fix: re-indent both blocks to match their true nesting depth.

packages/main/src/handlers/candidate-spec-routing.ts:197-200 and packages/main/src/core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:103 — dead 'agy-cli' lane left behind after its only construction site was deleted, leaving a silent-fallback maintenance trap. The diff removed `const primaryFailure = primary.length < 2; if (args.requestAgy || disagree || primaryFailure) attempts.push(await run('agy-cli'));` and the `requestAgy` parameter (verified via `git diff main...HEAD -- packages/main/src/core/candidate-spec-routing.ts`), so collectHostKeywordProposals now only ever calls run('codex-cli') and run('claude-cli') at :463. But HostKeywordProposal['host'] still declares 'agy-cli' (:103), and hostName() in the handler still ends with an unguarded `return 'agy'` (:200) reachable only for that now-unconstructable value. Failure scenario: hostName's final `return 'agy'` is a catch-all, not an equality check — a future maintainer adding a fourth host to the union without updating hostName gets that host silently mapped to 'agy' and passed to runHostRun as canonicalHost, which accepts 'agy' (host-run.ts:1689), so the wrong provider adapter launches instead of the code failing closed. Note the disagreement signal itself is NOT dead — `disagree` is still returned as hostDisagreement and consumed as the 'primary_host_disagreement' escalation flag (core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:468,:709; handlers/candidate-spec-routing.ts:363) — so only the third-host tie-breaker was removed. Fix: drop 'agy-cli' from the union and delete the branch, or make hostName's default an explicit throw rather than a fallback.

packages/main/src/core/finding-verify.ts:441-464 — the signReviewPass native branch (version 6) folds envelopeId into the signed digest WITHOUT the format re-validation that both sibling branches enforce, violating the project's documented 'runtime re-validation at every consumption point' convention (CLAUDE.md 'Handler 编码约定'). At :455 it writes `envelopeId: envelopeId ?? ''` into the digest with no check, whereas the managed branch immediately below rejects a malformed value at :466-468 ('managed evidence envelopeId must be a SHA-256 digest when present') and the legacy envelope branch rejects it at :493 (`if (!/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(envelopeId)) throw`). verifyReviewPass's native branch (:588-611) likewise reflects the value back unchecked, so a malformed id round-trips and verifies. This is the branch every current review_pass_set now takes (handlers/finding.ts:425 always issues a nativeEvidenceBinding, passed to signReviewPass at :459-461), i.e. the primary path is the one missing the check. Failure scenario: a caller supplying envelopeId 'not-a-digest' alongside a nativeEvidenceBinding gets a successfully signed and verifiable pass, while the byte-identical call on the managed or legacy path throws. Severity low rather than medium because it is defense-in-depth only: envelopeId is sourced from reviewRun.envelopeId (handlers/finding.ts:459) and independently cross-checked against the persisted envelope set (core/review-run.ts:665-670) and against the run binding at :1379-1386, so no known path reaches the gate with a malformed value. Fix: apply the same /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/ guard in the native branch.

packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts:173-175,249 — two dead exports in the new registry module. providerProcessSlotsDirExists (:173) has ZERO callers anywhere in packages/main/src or scripts (verified: `grep -rn 'providerProcessSlotsDirExists' packages/main/src scripts` excluding the defining file returns nothing; only a dist/*.d.ts declaration exists), and it duplicates the equally-uncalled hostRunSlotsDirExists at core/host-run.ts:2249. classifyProviderRegistryLock (:249) is exported but referenced only internally at :278; no external importer exists. Failure scenario is maintenance cost rather than runtime breakage: an exported symbol is part of the module contract, so a future refactor must preserve or deliberately break two entry points that nothing consumes, and the duplicate slots-dir predicate invites divergence between the two copies. Fix: delete providerProcessSlotsDirExists (and the duplicate in host-run.ts) and downgrade classifyProviderRegistryLock to a module-private function.

packages/main/src/core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts:28-47 — resolveCanonicalRuntimeProjectRoot forks an uncached `execFileSync('git', ['worktree','list','--porcelain','-z'])` subprocess on EVERY call, with no memoization anywhere in the module (verified: no Map/cache in the file). It is on hot paths: managed-host-run.ts:530,:534 make every managedHostRunsRoot/managedHostRunReceiptsRoot call fork git, and pathsFor (:588) routes through managedHostRunDirectory, so provider-process-registry.ts:170 forks once per admission decision before every provider spawn in lattice-dispatch.ts, planned-steps-executor.ts, autopilot-executor.ts and codex-review-leaf.ts, plus a second fork on the refusal path (provider-process-admission.ts:55). Worse, two loops call pathsFor PER ITERATION: scanManagedHostRunRuntime (managed-host-run.ts:2320) forks git once per run directory on every doctor invocation, and resolveManagedReviewProposalInvocation (:1727) forks once per candidate run directory on every provider proposal broker resolution. Failure scenario: a project with 50 retained managed-run directories pays 50 sequential `git worktree list` forks (each with a 2s timeout) on a single `lattice doctor`, and every provider spawn pays at least one fork of added pre-spawn latency. No correctness impact — the resolved value is stable for a given searchOrigin within a process. Fix: memoize the result per resolved searchOrigin, or hoist the canonical-root resolution out of the two per-iteration loops.

packages/main/src/core/provider-process-admission.ts:44-56 — the refusal-path diagnostic races itself, so an operator can be shown 'concurrency cap saturated' alongside an empty or short live-run list. acquireProviderProcessSlot (:44) takes the registry lock, fails to find a free slot, and releases it; then the ternary at :55 calls scanLiveProviderProcessSlots with a FRESH Date.now(), which takes the lock a second time. Between the two acquisitions any number of holders can release, so liveRuns can be shorter than cap — or empty — while admitted stays false. Failure scenario: cap=4, four slots held at acquire time so admission is refused; all four provider runs complete before the :55 scan; planned-steps-executor.ts:451-456 surfaces that liveRuns array in its concurrency_cap_exceeded block reason, so the operator reads a cap-exceeded refusal that lists zero live runs and cannot reconcile the two. Not a leak or oversubscription — the atomic wx create at provider-process-registry.ts:318-330 remains the real admission decision and is unaffected. Fix: capture the live descriptors inside the same lock acquisition as the failed acquire, or label the scan explicitly as a post-hoc sample in the surfaced diagnostic.
